name: tier-separable-runs
body:
Each test tier is independently selectable at the harness: the suite exposes three distinct, named, documented invocations — a unit-only run, an integration-only run, and an e2e-only run — in addition to the fast default gate. A tier selection runs ONLY tests of that tier: the unit-only invocation executes no integration test and no e2e test, the integration-only invocation executes no unit test and no e2e test, and the e2e-only invocation executes no unit test and no integration test.

The default gate is unchanged and must stay consistent with `requirements.requirement.fast-default-suite` and `requirements.requirement.e2e-final-gate-only`: a plain `cargo test` runs unit+integration only, stays seconds, and no e2e test is reachable through it, through the unit-only selection, or through the integration-only selection.

Tier membership is decided by `requirements.requirement.test-tier-definitions` / `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries` — the classification law is unchanged; this requirement adds selection, not new tier meaning. The three selections are a first-class harness capability (named and documented), not an ad-hoc filter string a caller must remember.

AC (review-checked):
- A unit-only run executes unit tests and NO integration or e2e test; an integration-only run executes integration tests and NO unit or e2e test; an e2e-only run executes e2e tests and NO unit or integration test (each selection's executed set contains only tests classified into its tier).
- The three selections are distinct, named, documented invocations of the harness (a documented command per tier), not a raw unfiltered `cargo test`.
- The default gate (plain `cargo test`) runs unit+integration and stays seconds, with e2e excluded.
- No e2e test is reachable by the default gate, the unit-only selection, or the integration-only selection.
